headline: Lockout talks show some signs of life despite cap fight
summary: Both sides keep talking and hardening positions on the cap and floor, with MLB offering a higher minimum and no escrow while the union rejects the rest.

headline: MLB files suit against the players' union
summary: The league asked a federal court to rule a lockout lawful and set aside its escrow plan, while the union called the filing frivolous and talks stayed stuck on the cap.

headline: MLB sues players' union, asking court to declare lockout is legal
summary: Clubs sued the MLBPA and eight player leaders in Manhattan, citing fear of an antitrust fight; the CBA ends Dec. 1 and a lockout is expected right after.

headline: Media revenue sharing advances, but only alongside a cap
summary: The union said it accepted equal pooling of local media revenue, while stressing that the league ties it to a salary cap it rejects.

headline: Union counters cap with equal sharing of all media revenue
summary: The players proposed pooling media money across all 30 clubs without a cap, as MLB pressed its cap plan and offered a $1 million minimum salary a week before the CBA expires.

headline: Union uses Manfred's own words against his cap pitch
summary: The MLBPA contrasted Manfred's 2021 and 2026 claims about the players' share of revenue as the lockout nears.

headline: Manfred says MLB will not compromise on a cap and floor
summary: A rundown of the commissioner's owners-meetings remarks, including his openness to bargaining through Thanksgiving.

headline: Manfred ends owners meetings with a cap ultimatum
summary: Owners will not move off a cap and floor, Manfred said, while leaving the lockout decision until the last moment and offering to bargain through Thanksgiving.
